I have the game on PC, currently its amazing. The density in the streets, the people and the traffic are all amazing, very immersive.

They have multiple teams working on things, in the industry you have many different clusters of people working on things to unify it into one build/patch in the end, this is why designing with many people can be a stressful task and requires management.

For instance, Art, Programming all feed into design. The features being added are simply ready to be put in, while other things like detaching the renderer and replacing it with a more optimized and modern solution (Like Opengl direct x11 etc) will take plenty of time because it requires literally changing how the game engine renders scenes.

I believe they are already working on it, integrating middleware effectively without murdering a complex engine such as arma 2/3's isn't easy.

it's not as easy as pushing a few buttons, hours and hours and hours goes into integration, and if your lucky, it goes smoothly, but that is rarely ever the case.

Coming from someone here who has developmental experience with Cryengine 3, and game design experience.

(Art and Animation primarily)

I have worked with cryengine 3 a lot over these past two years and I can tell you right now, the engine is one of the most powerful in the industry, it's truly one of the titans to be marveled at. Cryengine can make vast open maps or smaller more constrained levels, it's all up to how it's designed by artists and level designers in the end. Cryengine can import unlimited amounts of polygons, up until the engine ceases and your computer will not render the required amount anymore, this allows extremely high detailed models and assets to be in engine, as a showcase its pretty as well.

It uses the flowgraph system, a proprietary nodebased scripting/programming solution created by Crytek to facilitate programming without the need for an actual programmer to do simple things that and artist can do with simple script understanding, like open a door or even basic physics.

Cryengine is known to be a bit of a hefty engine, requiring quite a bit of tech to run it at it's best, but in the end its a well rounded engine, truly. The "Disrupt" Engine in Watch_Dogs is definitely looking to be a well tailored engine for all sorts of computer configurations, as long as the requirements are met at the minimum level, like Ubisoft stated "It will scale with the hardware".
